subject: Data residency anchoring & proposal for transient cross-region processing window
messages:
From: Emily Tran <emily.tran@aureliahealth.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@aureliahealth.com>, Aurelia Health Legal <legal@aureliahealth.com>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 10:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick clarifying questions on EU anchoring and short-term cross-region syncs

Hi Mina,

Thanks for the demo yesterday — the latency numbers were great. Before we move to procurement, our Legal and Infra teams have a couple of practical questions about the residency commitments in the DPA draft. We want to confirm two things:

1) Can Redwood guarantee that customer data for Aurelia Health will be anchored in the EU region for storage and inference by default? If so, what operations (e.g., backups, analytics, model telemetry) might be allowed to leave the EU transiently?

2) We understand a transient failover/sync window may be necessary for cross-region failover. What's the proposed maximum window for temporary cross-border processing, and do you have a playbook for notification/approval and audit evidence for those events?

Attached is a short list of questions from our privacy team (Aurelia_DPA_Questions.pdf).

Appreciate a short summary we can send to our internal reviewers.

Best,
Emily
Emily Tran
Senior PM, Product Privacy
Aurelia Health

(Attachment: Aurelia_DPA_Questions.pdf)

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Tran <emily.tran@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 27 May 2026 13:08:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick clarifying questions on EU anchoring and short-term cross-region syncs

Hi Emily — thanks for the note and the clear questions. Putting the short answers up front and then the proposed operational controls below so you can pick what you want to share with Legal/Infra.

Short answers:
- Yes: by default, customer data for Aurelia Health will be anchored within the EU region for both persistent storage and inference endpoints (model execution).
- Transient processing: Redwood supports limited, auditable transient cross-region processing for operational reasons (failover, DR, short-lived analytics jobs requested by the customer). We propose a maximum standard transient window of 72 hours for unplanned failover, but for most customers we recommend 48 hours as the default tactical maximum.

Operational controls and ask:
- Notification & approval: Redwood will send an automated incident notice to the customer's security contact and Legal Slack channel within 1 hour of the failover event. For planned maintenance that requires transient routing, we request 72 hours advance notice.
- Auditability: All transient events will be logged with a full event record (start/end timestamps, triggered route, affected shards, and operator id). Logs and a short incident summary will be available in the Console and via the shared link within 24 hours of the event closing.
- Subprocessors: See the attached subprocessor roster (subprocessor_roster_may2026.csv). Any subprocessor outside the EU used for transient processing will be listed and covered under the DPA subprocessor terms; we offer escrowed contractual commitments on request for named subprocessors.
- Data minimization during transit: Only the minimal KV/prefix cache + telemetry required to restore inference state will be transmitted during a transient synchronization; customer-configurable flags can reduce transmitted payload further (e.g., strip session metadata).

Proposed next steps:
1) If Aurelia agrees to a 48-hour operational default with an optional 72-hour exceptional window, Redwood will provide a DPA addendum with a clearly defined "transient cross-region processing" clause and an operational runbook.
2) Marissa (Legal) will supply the redline of the clause and we can iterate.
3) We will commit a sample incident log export (anonymized) for your Infra team to review.

I've attached the cross-region clause redline we typically use for customers as a starting point. Happy to jump on a 30m call to walk your team through the playbook.

Thanks,
Mina Haddad
Head of Product Partnerships, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

(Attachments: subprocessor_roster_may2026.csv)

Hi Emily / Mina — looping in Legal for the redline.

Marissa here — quick thoughts from a DPA perspective:
- The distinction between "anchoring" (storage/inference placement) and "transient processing" needs a precise definition in the DPA. Suggest language: "Transient cross-region processing": limited, time-bounded processing of customer data strictly for recovery, operator-requested maintenance, or customer-authorized telemetry, not for feature experimentation or broad analytics.
- Proposed default window: 48 hours. Any extension beyond 48 up to 72 hours requires an escalation (written approval) from the customer's security contact and a recorded justification in Redwood's incident tracker.
- Audit retention: we recommend Redwood commit to retain incident logs and exportable audit artifacts for 12 months by default (longer retention is available as a paid add-on).
- Subprocessor notice: Redwood must notify Aurelia of any new subprocessor outside the EU used for transient processing at least 30 days prior to activation (or provide an immediate justification for emergency activation with post-facto notice).

I've attached a redline of a transient- egresse clause for your counsel to review (Redwood_transient_egress_clause_redline.docx). Happy to take feedback and produce a clean addendum.

Marissa Cole
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Tom / Emily — quick follow-up answers inline and next steps below.

- Data transmitted: default behavior is to transmit only minimal state required to resume inference (KV deltas and lightweight prefix snapshots). Full embeddings or request payloads are not transmitted as part of the failover sync unless the customer explicitly enables full-session replication in their org settings. We can set Aurelia to deltas-only by default.
- Console evidence: I'll generate an anonymized incident export and a 1-page runbook showing the Console notification and an example audit export. Expect these in your shared Drive link by EOD today.

Next steps / timeline:
1) Redwood to deliver DPA addendum redline (Marissa) + anonymized incident export and 1-page runbook — ETA: EOD Thu 28 May.
2) Aurelia to review redline and get back with comment set — ETA: Mon 1 Jun.
3) Procurement kickoff and SOW packaging — target signature by Fri 5 Jun (subject to legal redline cadence).

I'll post the artifacts to the Drive link and ping you when done.

Thanks,
Mina
